results.evidence: `onClick={() => { duplicateInsight(insight as InsightModel, true); setScenePanelOpen(false) }}` closes the panel unconditionally. That closes it in overlay mode, so the sidebar no longer covers the copy. Whether closing also happens in the docked mode is what c3 covers. c1 itself looks satisfied, but I can't see how scenePanelOpen behaves in docked mode.
`duplicateInsight(insight as InsightModel, true)` is still called, with the same redirect argument. `setScenePanelOpen(false)` is added after it and does not replace or suppress it.

`setScenePanelOpen(false)` is called unconditionally, with no check on whether the panel is an overlay. There is no wide-screen guard, so on wide screens the panel's open state is set to false too. Whether that visibly hides a docked panel isn't shown, but the code doesn't condition the close on overlay mode.

The link is still `push(urls.resourceTransfer('Insight', insight.id!))`, with no short id passed. The patch instead fetches the short id on the transfer page via `api.get(.../insights/${props.resourceId}/)`. The navigation does not carry it.

`case 'Insight': return insightShortId ? urls.insightView(insightShortId) : urls.insights()`. Once the short id is fetched, Back resolves to the short-id view URL. The fetch reaches the numeric ID through the API, which the author assumed but did not check. The end result still matches the criterion.
When `insightShortId` is null (fetch failed, not loaded, or missing), `sourceResourceUrl` returns `urls.insights()`, the insights list.

The Dashboard case still returns `urls.dashboard(resourceId)` and the Survey case `urls.survey(resourceId)`. Nothing in the patch changes the URLs `urls.resourceTransfer` builds for those kinds, so they gain no extra parameter.

The card gets `className="p-6 @container"` and the layout is `flex flex-col @md:flex-row`. The illustration is wrapped as `
{illustration}
`. Below the @md container width the content stacks and the illustration is hidden. At or above it, the illustration sits beside the text.

result:
I fixed all three issues, but I haven't run anything, so none of it is tested or type-checked. I did not add or adjust any tests.

1. **Duplicate closes the sidebar.** `InsightPanelActions.tsx` now calls `setScenePanelOpen(false)` right after `duplicateInsight(...)`, so the new copy is visible on a narrow screen. I left the menu-bar Duplicate item in `InsightSceneMenuBar.tsx` alone. It sits in a dropdown, not the sidebar.

2. **Back link on the transfer page.** `ResourceTransfer.tsx` built the Back link with `urls.insightView(<numeric id>)`, which is `/insights/<number>` and doesn't load. The transfer flow is keyed by the numeric ID, so for insights the page now fetches the insight and builds `urls.insightView(short_id)`. That is the same link used elsewhere. If the fetch fails or hasn't finished, Back goes to the insights list. Your description didn't say where Back should go in that case, so that fallback is my choice.

   I did this with a `useEffect` and `api.get` in the component, not a kea loader. A loader would have meant editing the hand-written logic types. The request goes to `api/environments/<team>/insights/<numeric id>/`, and I assumed that endpoint accepts the numeric ID without checking the backend. If you'd rather have it in the logic, or have the transfer URL carry the short ID, say so.

3. **Subscriptions empty state.** In `SubscriptionOverviewComponents.tsx`, the featured `SubscriptionEmptyState` card is now a container-query context (`@container`). It stacks vertically when narrow and lays out as a row from `@md` up. The illustration is hidden in the narrow case, so it no longer sits beside the text. I haven't rendered it, and I didn't confirm that `@md` container variants are already used elsewhere in the repo. Check it in the modal Storybook story.
